items.title: Bob Watts Interview, 1963-02-28
items.q: The interviewee (Bob Watts) does not speak in the provided transcript. The mention of Melvin Green is made by the Interviewer, who states 'I rode with Louis Haney and Melvin Green'. There is no evidence in the text that Bob Watts personally knew, met, or collaborated with Melvin Green.

ctx.x: The paper said they was going down Cleveland to St. Benard, then back up on the uptown side, St. Benard, to Portris, South Portris, to Simon Bolivar. Through those pass up right on up Simon Bolivar. To Jackson, back Jackson to Magnolia. Down Magnolia to Melton-Mead. Back out Melton-Mead and Simon Bolivar, this band. That's what I read, see. Yeah. But they say it was all together different.

They made it up, I think, more or less by the route, because I caught them on a cell in Ohio Street. They made their turn at Louisiana. That's where I rode with Louis Haney and Melvin Green in the captain's car. Because I remember that, and I remember getting into the car. I remember a good bit.
Well, they went to Luzon Avenue.
